host.host_principal: The Owner's Windows account. QEMU runs as an ordinary user process: no service, no elevation, no installer. The strong tier buys a kernel boundary, not a principal boundary (profiles P8).

provider.name: qemu
provider.install_method: A2: tools/msys2_lock.py install downloads the locked MSYS2 packages, checks each sha256, validates every archive entry (the built-in tar.exe decodes them), writes regular files only under {qemu_prefix} (hardlinks materialised as copies) and verifies every installed file. No installer, no administrator rights, no registry or PATH change.
provider.whpx_in_build: MSYS2's qemu-common documentation (share/doc/qemu/msys2.readme.txt) shows '-accel whpx'; the pinned qemu-system-x86_64.exe contains the WHPX accelerator's messages, including 'WHPX: No accelerator found'. Runtime availability: observed on this host in F-03.2.1b (evidence/F-03.2.1b-provider-validation.md): -accel help lists whpx, and in the paused boot QMP query-accelerators reported {"enabled": "whpx"}. Inference: the WHPX partition and its vCPUs were set up without error, since QEMU stayed up, answered QMP and printed no WHPX: line.

accelerator.name: whpx
accelerator.reason: QEMU uses TCG when no -accel is given, and tries each listed accelerator in turn (qemu.org invocation, -accel). Exactly one -accel whpx, and no accel= on -machine, makes a missing WHPX a launch failure that the harness reports as TIER_UNAVAILABLE naming A1.

state_dir.rules: Named explicitly by the Owner on every invocation (contract section 11): outside the checkout, outside %USERPROFILE%, no comma (QEMU option syntax). Nothing in it is committed.

signature.evidence: https://cloud.debian.org/images/cloud/ states that for the current images 'the safest method is to download the image and checksum files over TLS from cloud.debian.org or cdimage.debian.org'; only the legacy OpenStack images carry SHA512SUMS.sign. The same SHA512SUMS was fetched from both hosts and was identical; the image's JSON manifest carries the same sha512.

image.check_before_launch: sha256 of the local file, immediately before every launch; a mismatch refuses the launch (profiles P9).

firmware.type: SeaBIOS (bios-256k.bin as shipped in the pinned QEMU package)
firmware.reason: The image boots by BIOS or UEFI (it ships grub-pc-bin and grub-efi-amd64). BIOS needs no per-instance writable firmware variable store. Other data files QEMU may load (ACPI and option ROMs) come from the same pinned package; the virtio-net option ROM is disabled (romfile=).

kernel.reason: The image's own bootloader and kernel boot; they are covered by the image digest.

generator.status: implemented and tested in F-03.2.2a; observed in F-03.2.2b: the Debian guest's cloud-init 25.1.4 accepted the volume (DataSourceNoCloud [seed=/dev/vdc], status done, no errors) on two instances

seed.record_at_create: sha256 of seed.iso in the launch record; the same inputs give the same digest.

profile_revision.record_at_create: git rev-parse HEAD of the checkout; create refuses when profiles/ has uncommitted changes.

ceilings.justification: Host: 32 logical CPUs, 62 GB RAM, about 750 GB free on D:. One guest takes 25 % of the logical CPUs and 16 GiB (about 26 % of RAM), leaving 24 CPUs and about 46 GB for Windows and the Owner's WSL VM (whose default ceiling is half of RAM). Disks are thin qcow2: an instance can grow to at most 160 GiB, so the state directory holds four instances at full allocation. Two instances at full memory beside a fully used WSL VM would overcommit RAM; the reference mode is one shared instance. These are the outer caps for decision 0001's per-conversation overrides; Moby's caps (F-04.1) sit inside them.

nested_virt_masking: -cpu max,vmx=off,svm=off. Observed at the configuration level in F-03.2.1b (evidence/F-03.2.1b-provider-validation.md): WHPX accepted the max model with these flags off; QOM vmx and svm are false on all 8 vCPUs, and filtered-features is all zero. Unobserved until F-03.2.2: the guest-visible CPUID; inside the guest, grep -c -E 'vmx|svm' /proc/cpuinfo must be 0.

guest_agent.reason: Management is SSH over the loopback forward. No virtio-serial device, so no QEMU guest agent channel (profiles P6).

guest_storage.contract: profiles P3, P4 (F-03.3.1): the guest's complete approved volume and mount table. inspect compares the effective table with it exactly: every observed mount must match an entry, and every entry not marked optional must be observed.
guest_storage.derivation: The block devices and directories follow launch.argv and the seed (profiles/seed/user-data.tmpl). The pseudo and tmpfs mounts are the Debian 13 genericcloud image's own (kernel and systemd), as observed by findmnt -J on a fresh guest of this profile on 2026-11-06 (F-03.3.1 reconnaissance guest f0331-r).

mounts.optional: mounted by the autofs trigger on first access
one per systemd service that is passed credentials; the set depends on the running services
the agent user's runtime directory, present while agent has a session
provisioned instances only (F-04.1): Moby's network-namespace handles, the host namespace ('default') while dockerd runs and one per running container
provisioned instances only (F-04.1): the root file system of a running container, under Moby's data root on scratch
provisioned instances only (F-04.1): a running container's /dev/shm

exchange.contract: profiles P4 and the lifecycle bindings 'exchange push' and 'exchange pull' (F-03.3.1).
exchange.transport: sftp.exe (Windows' built-in OpenSSH) over the management SSH forward, with identity.ssh_client_options, the per-instance key and no ssh_config (-F none).

provisioning.authority: decision 0006, 'Owner authorization (2026-11-06)', Part B: a single-use root step seeded by cloud-init, Moby and the agent-server image for inspection only, under the guest-validation conditions of decision 0003 as that authorization amends them. No guest network, no guestfwd, no host share and no launch.argv change.
provisioning.scope: slices (b) and (c): Moby (Debian docker.io and its closure), the pinned agent-server image, and the Agent Server release binary as a hardened systemd service under the system user openhands with its configuration and its two guest-generated secrets (agent_server).
provisioning.create: create --provision re-verifies the host stage of the lock (provision-fetch) and writes the manifest into the seed (profiles/seed/README.md, placeholder provision_manifest). An ordinary create writes an empty manifest: the seeded units carry ConditionFileNotEmpty on it and the trigger is never enabled.

upload.transport: sftp.exe over the management SSH forward, as agent, with the exchange's client options and the per-instance key (no new endpoint)

root_step.single_use: the trigger is disabled, stopped and its unit file removed in every outcome; the service refuses to run once RESULT.json or the staging directory exists

facts.use: Enabled by a successful root step. At every boot, after docker.service and aieh-agent-server.service, root writes a read-only report (docker version and info, the image store, containers, daemon.json, TCP listeners, Moby's sockets, kernel modules, and the Agent Server's binary, unit, process identity, data paths, engine endpoint, secret-file modes, secret fingerprints and start-up log with the secret values redacted and counted) that inspect reads as agent. It takes no input from the guest user and never writes a secret value.

moby.icc_rule: S-01.3.1: icc false is Moby's own control for the default bridge: no connection between two containers on it (observed before it: each conversation container reached the others' inner servers on 8000 and 8001). It does not touch the guest's own connection to a container's published loopback port (docker-proxy).

sysctl.content:
# AIEH (F-04.1): no IPv6 on Moby's bridge and veth interfaces (profiles P7)
net.ipv6.conf.docker0.disable_ipv6 = 1
net.ipv6.conf.veth*.disable_ipv6 = 1
sysctl.reason: Written before the install. Observed in the first provisioning run (F-04.1b): after the verification container ran, docker0 carried the IPv6 link-local fe80::42:c9ff:feaa:9805/64, which the P7 check 'IPv6 off unless listed' refuses. udev's systemd-sysctl rule applies these keys as each interface appears.

containerd_config.reason: Observed in the first provisioning run (F-04.1b): Debian's containerd ships config.toml (a conffile) with the CRI plugin enabled, and its streaming server listened on the guest's 127.0.0.1:41943, a TCP listener of Moby. Moby does not use CRI. The root step replaces the packaged file after the install (only when its md5 is the packaged one; a conffile cannot be written before dpkg without a prompt or a --force option) and restarts containerd and the daemon. The packaged file's other setting (the opt plugin path) is kept.

moby.socket_rule: profiles P6 (amended 2026-11-06): the guest's own Moby sockets, never a host socket. Every socket under /run/docker and /run/containerd is owned by root with group root or docker and not writable by others (connecting to a unix socket needs write permission); the declared ones have no access for others at all. agent is not in group docker and cannot connect.
moby.tcp_listeners: none: no hosts entry in daemon.json (unix socket only), containerd's CRI plugin off; no listener owned by dockerd, containerd or docker-proxy

image.rule: decision 0006 item 3: the image ID equals the locked config digest; after docker load the archive's placeholder tag is removed and only this local immutable tag remains
image.verify_run: docker run --rm --entrypoint true <local_tag>, as root inside the root step: proves the runtime without starting the agent-server entrypoint (slice (c))

agent_server.use: Inspection only (decision 0006, Owner authorization Part B): no LLM, no repository content, no untrusted workload. No conversation is created by F-04.1; F-04.2 creates the disposable one from the fixture below.

binary.source: provision lock release_binary (SHA256SUMS of the v1.60.1 release); copied from the verified staging copy, re-hashed, then the upload is deleted

user.name: openhands
user.rule: a system user with no login shell and a locked password, created by the root step; member of docker so that the server's docker CLI reaches the guest's own daemon socket. agent is never in docker (decision 0006 item 4).

service.bind_rule: The 1.60.1 entry point binds 0.0.0.0 by default once a session API key is configured (__main__.py), so --host 127.0.0.1 is explicit.
service.start: Type=exec; ExecStartPost waits for GET /ready on 127.0.0.1:8000 (200) with a 280 s ceiling, so the unit is active only when the server is ready and the boot-time facts report (ordered after it) sees its listener.

dependencies.rule: E-01.2.2 (findings F-1 and F-2): Requires= and After= on Moby and on the quiesce step, never Wants=, BindsTo=, Requisite= or an edge to the guard. Every start of the server (boot, systemctl start or restart, and Restart=on-failure) pulls a new start job for the oneshot quiesce step, which runs to completion first; if docker.service or the step does not succeed, the server's start job fails with result dependency, so the server neither runs nor listens. Moby's own start needs the container guard (its drop-in), so a failing guard stops all three.

hardening.justification: The server needs only: its own files under /srv/scratch/openhands (the one writable path), loopback TCP (its listener, and the loopback ports Moby publishes for conversation containers in F-04.2), and AF_UNIX to /run/docker.sock through the docker CLI it runs as a child. Containers are created by dockerd (root, outside this unit), so the unit needs no capability, namespace, device, kernel tunable or SUID binary; read-only mounts do not stop connect() to a unix socket. IPAddressDeny=any with IPAddressAllow=localhost refuses any non-loopback packet from the server's cgroup (defence in depth beside SLIRP restrict=on). Not set: MemoryDenyWriteExecute (the PyInstaller-built CPython and its native extensions are not qualified under it), PrivateNetwork (the listener must be reachable from the guest's loopback) and PrivateUsers (it would hide the docker group from the docker CLI).

quiesce.plan_leaf: E-01.2.2 (slice (c): the fix forward of finding F-2)
quiesce.use: The pinned 1.60.1 server, at every start, resumes in its own process every stored conversation whose base_state.json says running (ConversationService.__aenter__: hydration, the stored tool modules imported, the stored working_dir created and git-initialized), before any lease check and with no configuration to turn it off; the conversation store is the job's own bind, and a job can write running (evidence/E-01.2.2b-live-drills.md section 4). This root step runs before every server start and makes that path unreachable: no job process exists while it runs or when the server starts, and no stored record says running. It is a compensating control for the upstream limit fd-outer-server-local-recovery (security/inventory.json), not an upstream change.

actions.rule: docker ps --all --quiet, then docker rm --force of every container, then docker ps again: none may remain. The guest's Moby runs only the server's conversation containers (profiles P6, S-01.3.2), and the server's own start-up cleanup removes every owner-labelled container anyway (docker_runtime/registry.py cleanup_stale_containers), so no running work is lost that the server would keep. First, so that no job process can write while the records are read.

Each entry of provisioning.agent_server.config conversations_path, through directory-relative opens that never follow a link (every path component opened with O_NOFOLLOW, then openat-style access from a directory fd). An entry is acted on only when it is a directory and its meta.json and base_state.json (where present) are regular files with link count 1, owned by the service user's uid and primary gid, within the size bound. base_state.json execution_status running is rewritten to error in place (the same inode, owner and mode; every other value as parsed; upstream's own recovery outcome, openhands/sdk/conversation/state.py). JSON that does not parse as an object is left alone (the catalog drops such a record). An entry that fails any check, or whose meta.json id is not the UUID whose hex is the directory name, is moved aside, never deleted: renamed into the quarantine. An entry without meta.json is not a record (the catalog skips it) and is left alone.

quiesce.owner: provisioning.agent_server.user (uid and primary gid of openhands, the user conversation containers run as)

quarantine.rule: Created by the root step's agent-server-install step; a guest_storage directory of role agent-server-quarantine on the scratch disk, outside every agent-server directory, so the rename stays on one file system and the server's catalog (conversations_path) never reads it. The step refuses to run if it is not a root-only 0700 directory on the file system of the conversations path. Entries are named <hex id or entry>.<UTC time>.<random>; nothing in it is deleted by the step.

quiesce.invariant: zero containers before the server's ExecStart: the step ends with docker ps empty, and only the server creates containers
quiesce.journal: One line per run, prefixed 'aieh-agent-server-quiesce: ', a JSON object with counts and hex ids only (containers removed and remaining, entries, rewritten, quarantined with a reason code, unparseable, unchanged, not a record), never file content; the boot facts report this boot's last line.
quiesce.fail_closed: Any other failure (Moby unreachable, a container that remains, the conversations path or the quarantine not as declared, an I/O error) exits non-zero; the server's start job then fails with result dependency and Restart=on-failure does not retry it, so the server stays stopped until an operator acts.
quiesce.limit: fd-outer-server-local-recovery: the upstream defect stays in the pinned binary; when a pinned release skips local recovery for Docker-backed conversations, keeping or retiring this step is a recorded decision.
quiesce.check: check_profile validates this declaration against the seed template; inspect compares it with the boot facts (unit settings, the server's dependencies, the script, the quarantine, the last run and its order before the server's ExecStart)

config.mechanism: OPENHANDS_AGENT_SERVER_CONFIG_PATH (1.60.1 config.py CONFIG_PATH_ENV); OH_* variables override it, and the unit sets none of its fields. Non-secret: delivered in the seeded manifest and written by the root step.
config.caps_rule: decision 0001 s3: explicit per-conversation caps inside the guest ceilings. Each conversation container gets --memory 4g, --cpus 2.0 and --pids-limit 512 (registry.py _build_container); max_concurrent_runs 3 keeps three running conversations at 12 GiB of the 16 GiB and 6 of the 8 vCPUs, leaving the rest for the guest, dockerd and the server. A create request's container options replace the memory and CPU caps and are not capped by them (openapi ConversationContainerOptions): that 0001 s3 finding stays an obligation of F-04.2 and E-01.2.2.
config.not_configured: no LLM, no webhook, no session_api_keys or secret_key (they are secrets, in the environment file), no telemetry (exporter none, also the 1.60.1 default), no VSCode server and no tool preload (the browser preload would start chromium). enable_browser false (S-01.3.2): conversation containers get OH_ENABLE_BROWSER 0 by this setting, not only because the local tag is not the stock image's (launch.py container_browser_enabled).

agent_server.environment_rule: OH_PERSISTENCE_DIR is read by openhands-sdk get_user_persistence_dir, not by Config: it holds the runtime persistence (runtime-control and runtime-data of the Docker runtime) and the profile stores. TMPDIR keeps the PyInstaller extraction and the tmux directory on scratch (/tmp is a tmpfs).

secrets.generated: in the guest by the root step (python3 secrets.token_urlsafe(32), 43 characters each); never in the seed, the manifest, the upload or a log
secrets.delivery: EnvironmentFile= of the unit, read by systemd as root before it drops to openhands, so the file needs no access for openhands. The process environment (/proc/<pid>/environ) is readable only by openhands and root.
secrets.fingerprint: sha256 of 'aieh-secret-fingerprint/v1' + LF + the value: published in RESULT.json and the facts report so that host-side records can be scanned for the value without holding it

session_key.rule: profiles P5 (amended 2026-11-07): the per-instance session API key is the one guest-local secret exported, by SFTP as agent, into the instance directory only; destroy removes it with the instance. It is never logged, recorded or committed; records carry its fingerprint only.

listener.rule: profiles P7 (amended 2026-11-07): the guest-internal listener of the Agent Server, on the guest's loopback only; not forwarded to the host (the Agent Server hostfwd stays deferred, decision 0006).

fixture.purpose: The immutable POST /api/conversations body of the disposable conversation that F-04.2 creates: Docker runtime, a fixed conversation id, no initial message, no LLM credential, a bare agent with no tools, the server-provisioned workspace (/workspace, no host path) and no container override of the caps. F-04.1 does not send it.

openapi.check: tools/check_profile.py --openapi <downloaded openapi.json>: the file's sha256 must equal this pin (composition/lock/components.lock.json release_assets); the fixture is then validated against the schema with a standard-library JSON Schema subset. openapi.json is not committed (decision 0005).

conversations.use: The declared shape of every conversation container the Agent Server runs (one per Docker conversation, docker_runtime/registry.py _build_container of the locked 1.60.1 wheel), which inspect and conversation-smoke compare exactly with docker container inspect from the on-demand facts. Inspection only: the disposable conversation of the fixture, no LLM, no repository content, no untrusted workload (decision 0006, Owner authorization Part B).
conversations.owner_rule: The label's value is sha256(conversations_path + NUL + OH_PERSISTENCE_DIR)[:24] of the resolved paths (DockerConversationRegistry.__init__); the server lists and removes stale containers by it at start-up. Every container that carries the label must be one of this server's.
conversations.image: Config.Image is config.conversation_image (the local immutable tag) and .Image is the locked image ID (decision 0006 item 3); any other image ID is a stop condition.
conversations.user: Config.User is the uid:gid of provisioning.agent_server.user (registry.py runs --user os.getuid():os.getgid() of the server).
conversations.mount_policy: The effective Mounts list equals this list exactly ({conversation_hex} is the conversation id without hyphens; the image declares no volume). Every source is under the source root on the scratch disk: the conversation's own event store, its runtime home and the server-provisioned workspace (the fixture sends working_dir /workspace, so no caller-selected host path: decision 0001 s3). Never the Docker or containerd socket, Moby's data root, /etc/aieh, /var/lib/aieh or any other host path.
conversations.listener_rule: profiles P7 (amended 2026-11-07, F-04.2): while conversation containers owned by the Agent Server run, each may have exactly one listener on the guest's 127.0.0.1 at an ephemeral port (inside ip_local_port_range), owned by docker-proxy or dockerd and mapped to that container's port 8000 (registry.py publishes -p 127.0.0.1::8000). No other Moby listener, never a non-loopback bind, never forwarded to the host.
conversations.caps_rule: HostConfig Memory, NanoCpus and PidsLimit equal the config's conversation_container_memory, _cpus and _pids_limit (decision 0001 s3): the fixture sends no container override.

deviations.rule: registry.py always adds --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway; host-gateway resolves to the guest's docker0 address, not to the Windows host
registry.py passes no --network, so the container is on Moby's default bridge with NAT through the guest (no egress: the guest has no route out and SLIRP is restrict=on)

a create request's container.memory and container.cpus replace the server's caps and are not capped by them; the fixture sends neither, and conversation-smoke compares the effective caps with the config

conversations.deviation_rule: Recorded as evidence and carried to S-01.3.x and E-01.2.2; not failed here and not changed (upstream runtime behaviour).

facts.rule: On demand, root, read-only. agent creates the request file in the root:agent 0730 directory (it can create, not list); the path unit starts the oneshot reporter, which removes the file without reading it (its existence is the only input), runs no container command but docker ps and docker container inspect, and writes an agent-readable report of the containers carrying owner_label (environment by name only, every secret value counted and redacted), root's TCP listeners with the docker-proxy argv, the stored conversations (files, sizes, sha256, event ids and kinds; runtime control files by name and size) and the server's journal. At most 20 runs in 60 s (TriggerLimitBurst and StartLimitBurst); beyond that the units fail closed until the next boot.

admission.use: The management API admission of the outer Agent Server: who may reach its routes, with which credential, and what a refused request sees. Validation only: disposable conversations of the fixture (and one derived from it), no LLM, no repository content, no untrusted workload (Owner authorization of 2026-11-07, evidence/bootstrap-log.md).

routes.purpose: The route inventory and the dispatcher's allowlist: every route of the running 1.60.1 server (its /openapi.json) and every route the locked release binary registers outside that document (WebSockets, the Canvas App backend proxy, the documentation routes), each with its credential, class (public-read, management-read, privileged), dispatcher use and the expected refusal. guest.py admission-probe compares the live document with it and probes every route.

session_key.server_rule: 1.60.1 dependencies.py check_session_api_key on every /api router (401 HTTPException without or with a wrong key); WebSockets: first-message auth, close 4001 'Authentication failed'; a wrong key in the query or header refuses the handshake (403). Config.session_api_keys: an empty list means the server is unsecured, and empty values are dropped.
session_key.start_rule: ExecStartPre of the unit (as openhands, with the environment file): the server starts only when the session key and OH_SECRET_KEY are 43-character token_urlsafe values, distinct, and no other session-key variable (OH_SESSION_API_KEYS_<n> for n > 0, SESSION_API_KEY) is set; otherwise systemd never runs ExecStart, so a missing key fails closed instead of serving an unsecured API. It prints variable names only.

network.listener_rule: The management listener is 127.0.0.1:8000 only (listener above), and the unit's IPAddressDeny=any with IPAddressAllow=localhost drops any non-loopback packet of the server's cgroup: the agent network (Moby's default bridge) has no path to it.

guard.rule: Guest-level, because the Agent Server cannot express it: in the filter table's INPUT chain, a packet that arrives from a container bridge (docker0, br-+) and is not part of a connection the guest opened jumps to the chain, is logged (rate-limited, kernel log) and is refused: TCP with a reset, anything else with an ICMP port-unreachable. A container therefore reaches no listener of the guest itself at any of its addresses (host.docker.internal is docker0): not sshd, not systemd-resolved's LLMNR, not the management listener. Replies to the guest's own connections (docker-proxy to a container's port 8000) are RELATED,ESTABLISHED and pass. Forwarded traffic is the egress guard's (egress_guard, S-01.4).
guard.fail_closed: The drop-in makes docker.service Require and start After the guard: if the rules cannot be installed, Moby does not start and no conversation container can be created; aieh-agent-server.service Requires and starts After docker.service (E-01.2.2 finding F-1: it had Wants=, and the server served its API with Moby down), so its start fails with result dependency and the server stays stopped. The root step's admission step verifies the unit, the rules of both families and the bridge's enable_icc before the Agent Server is installed.

egress_guard.allowlist_rule: The endpoint classes this profile enables for containers: network.endpoints of class inference or provision without a deferred status. None is enabled, so the allowlist is empty and every new forwarded connection from a container bridge is refused. Its first entry belongs to S-03.x (inference, after the broker's Owner authorization); an entry sits between the RETURN and the LOG rule.
egress_guard.rule: Guest-level, in Moby's DOCKER-USER chain of the filter table (FORWARD jumps to it first): a packet that enters from a container bridge (docker0, br-+), leaves by another interface and is not part of an established connection jumps to the chain, is logged (rate-limited, kernel log, this prefix) and is refused: TCP with a reset, anything else with an ICMP port-unreachable. A container therefore opens no connection out of the guest: not to SLIRP's 10.0.2.2 (the host's loopback) or 10.0.2.3, not to an unconfigured guestfwd address, not to an off-guest address, IPv4 or IPv6. Traffic between two containers of one bridge does not leave it and stays with icc false (the peer container); connections to the guest itself stay with the container guard (INPUT). Off-link destinations have no route in the guest (SLIRP restrict=on gives no default route), so the guest's routing answers them before FORWARD (network unreachable): that is topology, not the guard. With a route present the guard refuses them too: proved by the route-present falsification (falsification below; S-01.4 fix-forward), where 1.1.1.1:443 and 8.8.8.8:53 (TCP and UDP) were refused from both jobs with the guard's counters rising by exactly the attempts and its log showing the uplink as OUT.
egress_guard.dockerd: The guard runs before docker.service and creates DOCKER-USER when it is absent. It ends DOCKER-USER with the RETURN rule that Moby 26.1 adds when none exists, so Moby leaves the chain unchanged, and Moby re-inserts FORWARD's jump to DOCKER-USER at the top (IPv4). Moby 26.1 does not manage ip6tables (ip6tables off), so the guard's own FORWARD jump stands there. ip-forward is not set false (S-01.4 ruling R5).
egress_guard.fail_closed: Installed by the same script and unit as the container guard: if any egress rule cannot be installed the unit fails and docker.service, which Requires it, does not start. The root step's admission step (after Moby's first start), the boot facts (after docker.service at every boot, with the rules the guard printed before Moby started) and inspect verify the chain, the hook rules and FORWARD's first jump in both families.

falsification.create: create --provision --egress-falsification only: the manifest carries validation.egress_route and the root step enables the path unit; an ordinary provisioned guest has neither
falsification.rule: Validation only. On agent's request file, root adds a temporary IPv4 default route via SLIRP's gateway on the uplink (refused if a default route exists), reports the routes before and with it, waits for the off request or the ceiling, then always deletes the route and reports the routes after (state removed, or REMAINS). SLIRP restrict=on still refuses every off-host packet, so containment stays double while the route exists. job-access-probe uses it to prove that the egress guard, not the missing route, refuses off-link egress the moment a route exists; it removes the route in a finally-style cleanup and verifies it is gone.

rejection.http: 401 {"detail": "Unauthorized"} for every key-gated route, without a key or with a wrong one; the server logs 'HTTPException 401 on <method> <path>' at info level
rejection.websocket: first-message auth: accepted, then close 4001 'Authentication failed' (logged 'WebSocket first-message auth failed: ...'); a wrong key in the query or header: the handshake gets 403 ('WebSocket authentication failed: invalid API key')
rejection.app_backend: the Canvas App backend proxy answers 503 (ingress not configured) and refuses its WebSocket handshake (403)
rejection.network: from a container bridge: a TCP reset (connection refused) from the guard, logged with the prefix in the kernel log; the management listener refuses at every non-loopback address (no socket bound there)
rejection.dispatcher: the trusted dispatcher sees a 401 with no further detail for a missing or wrong key, a 2xx for an admitted request, a 422 for an invalid body, and a 503 'Conversation service is not available' or 'server is in deferred-init state' while the server is not ready; it never retries a 401 with another credential

dispatcher.bootstrap: No dispatcher exists. During bootstrap its role is performed by the Owner's account through tools/guest.py over the instance's SSH forward as the operator login agent, which reads the session key from its file inside the guest; no agent workload ever has that login or its SSH key.
dispatcher.owner_ui: planned (decision 0013, Proposed): the Owner UI never holds the management key; it reaches an engineering session only with that conversation's runtime credential, issued by the dispatcher, over a dispatcher-owned local forward bound to host 127.0.0.1 (U-01.2, E-01.3.x). Each such forward is a new host port and needs a recorded Owner approval. No host forward of the Agent Server exists (decision 0006).

admission.probe: tools/guest.py admission-probe on a running provisioned instance (Task target guest:admission-probe)

jobs.use: The job environment of builder and reviewer runs: each conversation container the guest's Agent Server creates (the Overseer's ruling for S-01.3.2). No engine socket, no engine API, no management route and no management, Owner, admin or bot credential is reachable from it. Declared here, checked per container by inspect (provisioning / conversation containers) and proved from inside two disposable conversation containers by tools/guest.py job-access-probe. Validation only: disposable conversations of the fixture, no LLM, no repository content, no untrusted workload (Owner authorization of 2026-11-07).

sources.server: docker_runtime/registry.py _build_container of the locked 1.60.1 wheel, read as data: docker run -d --rm --user <server uid>:<gid> --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --ulimit core=0 --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway --label <owner> --name agent-server-conversation-<uuid4> -p 127.0.0.1::8000, -e for the forwarded names only, exactly the three -v binds, --memory, --cpus and --pids-limit. These flags are hard-coded: Config offers the image, the three caps, the start-up timeout and the browser (enable_browser, conversation_image_has_browser), and no option for capabilities, security options, mounts, network, extra hosts, a read-only root or the user.
sources.server_config: enable_browser false and the explicit caps and image of provisioning.agent_server.config: the minimal job options the locked server's own configuration supports.
sources.moby: Moby 26.1.5 defaults that the server does not set, as observed: the builtin seccomp profile, AppArmor docker-default, private IPC and cgroup namespaces, no device, the default bridge. daemon.json no-new-privileges true is the daemon-wide default behind the server's own flag, and icc false (S-01.3.1) separates the containers; required_security_options names the daemon defaults the job profile relies on.

host_config.rule: docker container inspect of each container (the on-demand root facts) has exactly these HostConfig values and AppArmorProfile; null matches an empty list, object or string. SecurityOpt is exactly no-new-privileges, so seccomp, AppArmor, the SELinux label and the system paths keep the daemon's confined defaults and are never unconfined or disabled. HostConfig.Mounts is empty: the only mounts are the three declared binds (provisioning.agent_server.conversations).

environment.rule: By name only, case-insensitive: Config.Env and every process environment readable inside the container carry no engine variable and no credential name but the conversation's own two keys (cred-conversation-keys); the terminal's environment carries neither (the SDK's sanitized_env).

process.rule: Inside the container, as its default user (the server user's uid:gid, no supplementary group): CapInh, CapPrm, CapEff, CapBnd and CapAmb all zero, NoNewPrivs 1, Seccomp 2 (filter), AppArmor docker-default enforced. Root is not obtainable: the image's sudo and su are setuid root, the kernel ignores setuid under no_new_privs (sudo refuses) and su needs a password; with an empty bounding set uid 0 would still hold no capability. If root were obtainable, the probe repeats its socket and TCP attempts as root.

jobs.socket_rule: Inside a job every listed path is absent (ENOENT). Every socket file on the container's filesystem and every bound name in its /proc/net/unix (abstract names included) is tried as well; a connection that answers the Docker Engine API's /_ping is a stop condition.

host_alias.rule: 10.0.2.2 is SLIRP's alias of the host's loopback: the instance's SSH forward and QMP ports and the host Gitea's 127.0.0.1:13300 (F-06.1) must be unreachable from a job, as every port there (restrict=on, no guestfwd: F-03.3.2).

jobs.tcp_rule: From inside a job: the engine ports, the management listener's port and the published conversation ports at host.docker.internal and at each guest address, and the engine ports on the container's own loopback, are refused (the container guard's reset for the guest, nothing listening on the container's loopback); the host alias ports and the engine ports at 10.0.2.2 and 10.0.2.3 are refused (SLIRP's reset); the peer container does not answer (icc false). A connection to an engine port, the management listener or a host service is a stop condition. Control: the container's own inner server answers on 127.0.0.1.
jobs.routes_rule: From inside a job, every route of the admission inventory (admission.routes) at the management listener's port of host.docker.internal and each guest address, without a key and with the conversation's own inner key: no connection. Any HTTP answer from the outer listener is a stop condition.
jobs.token_rule: No management, Owner, admin or bot credential in a job, searched by name and fingerprint, never by value: no credential file name (credential_files) and no .docker/config.json; the fingerprints of the outer session key and OH_SECRET_KEY (aieh-secret-fingerprint/v1 over every 43-character token of every readable file up to 8 MiB and of every readable process environment and command line) and every Gitea token fingerprint given to the probe (sha256: and 16 hex digits over every 40-hex token) are absent. Control: the scan finds the conversation's own key fingerprint in its process environment.

deviations.host-gateway: Carried: registry.py adds --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway unconditionally and Config has no option to remove it. Moby's host-gateway-ip would retarget the name, not remove it. The name resolves to the guest's docker0, where the container guard refuses every port.
deviations.no-network-none: Narrowed by S-01.4: the NAT path out through the guest is refused by the egress guard (admission.network.egress_guard), with no route out for off-link addresses and SLIRP restrict=on behind it. The absence of --network none is re-tested by S-02.1 and S-02.2.

jobs.fail_closed: No job control depends on a boot step to keep a socket or route closed: the engine sockets are absent from a job because the locked server mounts exactly three binds (a different binary is refused by its sha256 at provisioning); no_new_privs is set twice (the server's flag and daemon.json); without the container guard Moby does not start (S-01.3.1); without a valid key the server does not start (S-01.3.1); Moby has no TCP listener (no hosts in daemon.json, CRI off) and the host aliases are closed by SLIRP restrict=on in launch. A missing or loosened control is reported by inspect (Moby daemon, management API admission, conversation containers) and by this probe.

ci.statement: No CI runner exists (fd-ci-runner-unpinned); this leaf builds no runner and no CI profile. The runner containment profile is Q-02.2.1, proved by Q-02.2.2 and by Q-02.3.2's hostile job. The constraints below are declared, unverified requirements carried to those leaves.

constraints.rule: no engine socket (Docker, containerd, Podman, BuildKit) and no engine TCP endpoint reachable from a job
no management key, Owner, admin or bot token in a job's environment or readable filesystem
no privileged mode, added capability, device or host namespace
no host-path mount beyond the scoped workspace

jobs.probe: tools/guest.py job-access-probe on a running provisioned instance (Task target guest:job-access-probe)

network.posture: restrict=on and ipv6=off. The guest reaches nothing on the host or outside except through the explicit forwards below (qemu.org invocation: restrict=on 'does not affect any explicitly set forwarding rules'). Qualified by F-03.3.2: with a default route, resolvers, an IPv6 address and an IPv6 default route installed by guest root, every probed IPv4, ICMP, DNS, IPv6, host-LAN and host-loopback path was denied, also from a network namespace behind guest NAT, while one test guestfwd to a 127.0.0.1 listener carried a nonce exchange from both.
network.ipv6_statement: IPv6 is off at the enforcement point (ipv6=off): SLIRP handles no IPv6 at all. The guest kernel has IPv6 enabled but no address on the NIC (addr_gen_mode 1, accept_ra 0, network-config dhcp6 false, link-local []). With fec0::15/64, a default route via fec0::2 and static neighbour entries sending IPv6 frames to SLIRP's MAC (all added by guest root in F-03.3.2), every IPv6 probe timed out while the NIC's tx counter rose. No IPv6 endpoint is listed.

enforcement_point.mechanism: QEMU SLIRP restrict=on with ipv6=off. Guest-to-host traffic only through explicit guestfwd rules, each to a listener on 127.0.0.1; host-to-guest only through hostfwd bound to 127.0.0.1.
enforcement_point.method: tools/guest.py netprobe (test only; decision 0003, 'Owner authorization: network validation'): a disposable guest whose seed adds the pinned root probe and whose -netdev adds one guestfwd=tcp:10.0.2.100:7000-tcp:127.0.0.1:<test listener port>, beside a TCP and a UDP decoy on 127.0.0.1 that are not forwarded. Machine verdict: profiles P7 in inspect.
enforcement_point.observed_behaviour: With restrict=on, SLIRP answered a guest TCP SYN to any address other than the guestfwd address and port with a reset (Connection refused, about 0 s), including public IP literals, 10.0.2.2 (the host-loopback alias), 10.0.2.3 and the host's LAN address; it dropped UDP (DNS included) and off-link ICMP without a reply; it answered ICMP echo to 10.0.2.2 itself (no host socket); it dropped IPv6 frames (timeouts). No connection or datagram reached either decoy or the test listener's host port, and the listener's only peer was the QEMU process's guestfwd chardev.
limits: Containers were approximated by a Linux network namespace with a veth pair and iptables MASQUERADE in the guest (Docker's default-bridge shape); Docker itself is not in the image and was not installed (S-02.x tests a real container).
IPv6 was tested from the guest's root namespace only; the namespace has no IPv6 route (Docker's default bridge has none either).

A guestfwd chardev is one connection opened by QEMU at start (qemu.org invocation); after its listener stops it stays disconnected, and the QEMU process keeps a bound, non-listening client socket. An endpoint's broker must therefore run before the guest starts and for its whole life.
SLIRP's own ICMP echo reply for 10.0.2.2 and 10.0.2.3 remains (no host socket is involved).

permitted.observed: SSH exec, exchange push and exchange pull succeeded in the validation guest (with guest-root routes in place) and in an ordinary guest (F-03.3.2 cycles f0332-p, f0332-o).
Answered on 127.0.0.1 only; refused from the guest at 10.0.2.2 and on the host's LAN address and ::1.

permitted.path: guest 10.0.2.100:7000 to host 127.0.0.1:<test listener> (guestfwd; validation instances only, not in launch.argv)
permitted.observed: HELLO/NONCE/ECHO exchanged from the guest and from the namespace behind guest NAT; the listener logged both nonces matched, from the QEMU process's chardev connection only.

denied.path: public IPv4 literals 1.1.1.1:443/80, 8.8.8.8:53, 9.9.9.9:443, deb.debian.org's address :80/:443, with a default route
denied.observed: refused (reset from SLIRP), guest and namespace

denied.path: ICMP echo to 1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8 and the host's LAN address

denied.observed: udp: no reply; tcp: refused; name resolution through the guest resolver: timeout (40 s), guest and namespace

denied.path: host loopback through 10.0.2.2: the SSH-forward, QMP, test-listener and TCP-decoy ports
denied.observed: refused; no connection in the decoy or listener log, guest and namespace

denied.path: host loopback through 10.0.2.2: the UDP decoy
denied.observed: no datagram in the decoy log, guest and namespace

denied.path: the host's LAN address on the same ports, TCP and UDP
denied.observed: refused / no datagram, guest and namespace

denied.path: IPv6: public literals (TCP, ICMP, DNS), fec0::2 and fec0::3 (SLIRP's IPv6 defaults), and the host's global and ULA addresses on the forwarded and decoy ports, with an IPv6 address and default route

endpoints.purpose: QMP (lifecycle and inspect); host-side only, not reachable from the guest
git bundle transfer by SFTP over the management SSH forward

endpoints.status: deferred: the brokered endpoint does not exist yet, and enabling a guestfwd in this profile needs separate Owner authorization (decision 0003, 'Owner authorization: network validation')
endpoints.mechanism: guestfwd=tcp:<guest address>:<port>-tcp:127.0.0.1:<broker port> to a host-side broker (the mechanism qualified by F-03.3.2)

endpoints.status: deferred: no allowlisting proxy exists yet, and enabling a guestfwd in this profile needs separate Owner authorization (decision 0003); phase-limited

network.port_allocation: {ssh_port} and {qmp_port} are free ports on 127.0.0.1 chosen at create and kept in the launch record.
network.local_exposure: Loopback ports are reachable by any local process of any user on the host; disclosed, not prevented (Python's standard library has no AF_UNIX socket on Windows, so QMP uses loopback TCP).

identity.ssh_key: ed25519, generated at create with Windows' built-in OpenSSH ssh-keygen into {instance_dir}/ssh/; never ~/.ssh.
identity.host_key_trust: Fingerprints read from cloud-init's block on the serial log ({instance_dir}/serial.log), written to {instance_dir}/ssh/known_hosts.
identity.machine_id: Generated by the guest's systemd at first boot of a fresh overlay; uniqueness observed in F-03.2.2.

bindings.preflight: Read-only capability report: OS and arch; state directory named, existing, outside the checkout and %USERPROFILE%; provider binaries match their sha256; 'qemu-system-x86_64 -accel help' lists whpx; the image file matches its sha256. Each failure names its Owner act (A1, A2, A3).
bindings.create: Refuse if {instance_dir} exists. Create it; generate the SSH key; check the image sha256; qemu-img create the root overlay (40 GiB, backing the pinned image) and the scratch disk (120 GiB); generate seed.iso; allocate ports; write launch.json (every boot input with its digest, the argv, the profile revision); launch QEMU detached.
bindings.start: Relaunch from launch.json after re-checking every digest in it.
bindings.stop: QMP system_powerdown; after stop_timeout_s, QMP quit; if the process still runs, terminate that process id only.
bindings.destroy: Stop with force if running, then delete {instance_dir} only. Absent: succeed and report absent. The image, the provider and every other path are untouched.
bindings.recreate: destroy, then create with the same name and profile.
bindings.inspect: QMP query-version, query-cpus-fast, query-memory-size-summary, query-block, query-named-block-nodes, query-pci, query-chardev; qemu-img info of root and scratch; guest probes over SSH per profiles P1-P12; labelled per profiles P11. P3 and P4 compare the guest's mounts, disks, block nodes and directories with guest_storage exactly. P5 plants a synthetic sample of each Owner class in the scratch directory, collects the guest's /etc, homes, scratch, cloud-init files, logs and process environments (as agent) to the host, scans them there with the seed and the serial log, then removes the sample; with --canaries it also searches for a canary set planted in the create process. P6 checks virtio channel devices, vsock, host-management socket paths, environment and the guest's socket inventory, and QMP reachability from the guest. check-surfaces is the F-03.3.1 startup test: PASS only when P3 to P6 all PASS.
bindings.exec: ssh with identity.ssh_client_options to agent@127.0.0.1 -p {ssh_port}. Operator and provisioning only; never offered to agents.
bindings.exchange push: A git bundle of a bounded snapshot, copied by SFTP into /home/agent/exchange. Implemented (F-03.3.1): exactly one local branch, as a complete bundle with no prerequisites, within exchange.push (commits, bytes); built read-only from the named repository with git under no system or global configuration; header, pack checksum and git bundle verify checked; put under a new name (.partial, then rename) and its guest sha256 compared.
bindings.exchange pull: A git bundle and evidence copied by SFTP into a harness-owned staging directory under {state_dir}; never into the Owner's repositories. Implemented (F-03.3.1): one regular file of /home/agent/exchange within exchange.pull, into exchange.host_staging/inbound, sha256 compared with the guest's; a bundle is checked (header, pack checksum) and fetched into a fresh bare repository in the staging directory (after the pushed bundles when it has prerequisites), its references compared with its header, then git fsck --strict. Staging is inside the instance directory, so destroy removes it.

launch.notes: QMP is the one monitor, created with -object monitor-qmp on the loopback socket chardev (QEMU 11.1 deprecates -mon). No USB controller, audio device, display, VGA, monitor (HMP), file share, 9p, SMB or virtio-serial device is created: -nodefaults removes the defaults and none is added. The root overlay's backing node is bound explicitly to the pinned image, so the overlay header's backing path is not trusted.
